body: Yes, it is happening I also faced with this issue, 4.7.1

I can reproduce this with the Godot 4.7.2 .NET build. It happens on Linux, macOS and Windows, with .NET 9 and .NET 10.

Repro project and a GitHub Actions workflow that runs it: https://github.com/tom-tgr/godot-123707-repro

**The problem**

`Variant.Disposer.Dispose()` is not safe to call twice. The second call frees the native value again, and then throws "Disposable not registered". If the second call runs on the finalizer thread or on a normal `Thread`, nobody can catch the exception, so the game crashes.

`GodotObject` already protects against this with `if (_disposed) return;`. `Variant.Disposer` does not. `Godot.Collections.Dictionary` has the same problem, and probably `Array`, `StringName` and `NodePath` too.

**What happens on the second Dispose**

- On the main thread: Godot logs an error and the game keeps running.
- Inside `Task.Run`: nothing is logged, but the native value is still freed twice.
- On a normal `Thread`: the game crashes.
- On the finalizer thread: the game crashes. A common way to hit this is a class that disposes its `Variant` fields in `Dispose(bool)` without checking `disposing`. That crashes every time.

**Crash without any Dispose in game code**

In one test, worker threads parse JSON into `Variant`s and send them to the main thread with `CallDeferred`. The game code never calls `Dispose`. Sometimes it still crashes, with the same stack shape as in this issue, but from `Dictionary`:

```
System.ArgumentException: Disposable not registered. (Parameter 'weakReference')
   at Godot.DisposablesTracker.UnregisterDisposable(...)
   at Godot.Collections.Dictionary.Dispose(Boolean disposing)
   at Godot.Collections.Dictionary.Finalize()
   at System.GC.RunFinalizers()
```

I saw this twice so far, once on Linux and once on macOS. I don't know yet what disposes the `Dictionary` the first time.

**Possible fix**

Make `Dispose` safe to call more than once, like `GodotObject` already is:

- the first call frees the native value and unregisters;
- later calls do nothing;
- the finalizer never throws.

If this is fine, I can open a PR.
